title: Elazar ben Dinai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mishnah Sotah 9:9 preserves his name disparagingly: when murderers multiplied, the broken-necked-heifer ceremony ceased. Elazar ben Dinai, formerly called Techinah ben Perishah, came to be called ben HaRatzchan, son of the murderer. Ketubot 27a also mentions “Ben Donai’s wife.” Tosafot Yom Tov cites Rabbi Zanvil’s proposed reading, “At first [he was called] ben Perishah.”

notes.text: The supplied כן/בין and ובן are malformed forms in this passage; the complete Mishnah has a single man formerly called Techinah ben Perishah. Tosafot Yom Tov cites Rabbi Zanvil Katz’s proposal to read תחלה, at first, instead of תחינה, but then explicitly rejects that proposal. The source summary quotes the proposal without that rejection.
The consulted Mishnah Sotah 9:9 writes Eliezer ben Dinai, while Hyman’s notice writes Elazar. The name forms are preserved separately.
